title: Rule2DRC: Benchmarking LLM Agents for DRC Script Synthesis with Execution-Guided Test Generation
claim: A benchmark task bundles a rule, ground-truth script and labeled layouts, and agent outputs are scored by executing them against those layouts.
layout: 2 regions: stacked task data left, agent-to-engine flow right; arrows between
description: The figure shows one Rule2DRC task and how it is evaluated. A large stacked-page panel on the left holds a natural language rule ("Pad must be inside M4 and enclosed by M4 by at least 0.850 µm"), the ground-truth DRC script as colored code, and a fan of chip layout thumbnails with a m4/pad legend. Each layout carries a green "No violation (0)" or orange "Violation (1)" label tab. On the right, an arrow carries the rule r_i into a blue LLM Agent box, which loops with a yellow DRC Engine tool box. The agent emits a generated script in a code box. That script goes down into a second DRC Engine box, which also takes the layouts x_ij and outputs a stack of evaluated labels. Math notation labels every element, and the eye lands first on the left rule and script panel.
caption: Overview of the Rule2DRC benchmark. Each task includes a natural language (NL) design rule $r_i$, a ground-truth design rule checking (DRC) script $c_i$, a set of evaluation chip layouts $(x_{ij})$, and design rule violation labels for each layout $\phi(x_{ij}, c_i)$. An LLM agent $f(\cdot)$ generates an executable DRC script from the NL description, using the DRC engine as a tool. We evaluate the generated script by running it on the evaluation layouts and comparing its violation outputs with the outputs of the ground-truth script.
abstract: Manufacturable chip layouts must satisfy thousands of geometry-based design rules, and design rule checking (DRC) enforces them by running executable DRC scripts on layouts. Translating natural language rules into correct DRC scripts is labor-intensive and requires specialized expertise, motivating LLM agents for DRC script synthesis and debugging. However, existing benchmarks have small evaluation sets and often evaluate scripts by code similarity rather than execution correctness, and prior machine learning-based methods either ignore execution feedback or require labeled test layouts as agent's input. To this end, we introduce Rule2DRC, a large-scale benchmark for DRC script coding agents with 1,000 rule-to-script tasks and 13,921 evaluation chip layouts for execution-based scoring. Rule2DRC provides an evaluation pipeline that measures functional correctness via DRC execution outcomes without requiring evaluation layouts as input to the agent. We also propose SplitTester, a tester agent for program selection that uses execution feedback to generate discriminative test cases and separate previously indistinguishable candidate scripts, substantially improving Best-of-N selection performance in this domain. We release the code at https://github.com/snu-mllab/Rule2DRC.
